events.outcome: CTExcel UK and its Back to China SIM Retention Plan are current. Community evidence repeatedly reports a 90-day activity rule for some no-plan accounts but also plan-dependent retention and conflicting post-plan behavior. The provider-visible pages do not cleanly expose current retention eligibility, price and post-expiry mechanics, so no universal lifecycle or annual keep cost is asserted.

events.productCohort: New CTExcel UK £11 promotional annual eSIM purchased online; United States-model iPhone; China-side first setup
events.scope: OP paid, received QR, downloaded eSIM profile but failed cellular first activation while physically in China; eSIM later deleted; no target-app SMS test
events.outcome: One buyer reports eSIM profile/phone number downloaded, activation failed, customer service denied refund citing China location and requested UK passport and selfie for a reissue. These are OP-reported support conditions for this reissue, NOT universal initial KYC, a verified provider-wide refund rule, or proof any bank OTP failed.

events.productCohort: New CTExcel UK £1 physical SIM on Android with Windows Wi-Fi network preparation, not a new annual eSIM
events.scope: Self-described mainland physical-SIM setup using non-provider-authorized UK-network conditions and Wi-Fi Calling; article is partly tutorial/reports earlier sources; no independently named-app OTP receipt
events.outcome: OP claims physical SIM Wi-Fi Calling-led activation was possible after manually preparing a UK-like network environment. OP expressly says this is not an official mainland activation path. This does not establish legal/compliant first tower attach for a new eSIM, guaranteed China activation, or Telegram/WhatsApp/bank verification SMS.

events.productCohort: CTExcel UK annual eSIM purchased online, buyer abroad, dispute channel HSBC HK
events.scope: Buyer reports eSIM activation failure, an unanswered merchant refund email, then started payment dispute; no verified dispute conclusion, first tower attach or target service SMS result
events.outcome: A separate author reports failed annual eSIM activation and filing a Hong Kong bank payment dispute. Their original thread explains steps and a 6–8 week expectation, but does NOT establish actual recovered funds or a universal legal cancellation entitlement.

data.acquisitionSummary: CTExcel UK remains a current EE-hosted UK-China mobile route with UK SIM bundles, annual China data plans and a provider-listed Back to China SIM Retention Plan. Current community reports include purchase and activation from China, with network/IP/eSIM friction in some cases.

keep.action: Provider currently exposes a Back to China SIM Retention Plan. Community evidence conflicts: some users report roughly 90-day activity for no-plan accounts while plan users follow plan-specific retention. Exact eligibility, current price and post-plan clock are not cleanly provider-reconciled, so no universal interval or annual cost is modeled.

data.chinaActivation: Current first-hand community reports show China-side purchase/activation and service use can work, but some users report UK-network/IP or eSIM setup friction. Treat China-first activation as operationally evidenced but not uniformly guaranteed.
data.kyc: Current provider pages reviewed here do not establish a universal identity/KYC rule for all CTExcel UK acquisition cohorts.
data.payment: Current official ordering/account paths exist; exact foreign-card acceptance and retention-plan payment execution were not independently normalized.
data.roamingSms: Current community evidence supports China-side signal, SMS/number use and support recovery. Service-specific OTP reliability and long-term roaming enforcement remain evidence-scoped.
data.refund: A 2026 first-hand signal-loss case reports fast official support recovery; broader replacement/refund outcomes remain unquantified.
data.holdReason: The provider confirms a current Back to China retention product, but exact eligibility, price and post-expiry rules are not cleanly extractable; community reports also conflict on no-plan 90-day activity versus plan-dependent retention.
data.tariffSummary: Current UK-China plans and retention service exist, but this review intentionally does not publish a single annual keep cost or universal 90-day lifecycle.
guideSteps: Choose the exact CTExcel plan/retention product before relying on any lifecycle rule.
Do not generalize a community 90-day activity report across plan cohorts.
Preserve China activation/support incidents and service-specific OTP outcomes as separate evidence.

data.acquisitionSummary: CTExcel UK offers physical SIM and annual eSIM products. A £1 physical-SIM user reports China-side setup only using an unofficial Wi-Fi Calling/network workaround; TWO independent new-annual-eSIM buyers report paid QR delivery or order receipt but overseas first activation failed. A downloaded eSIM profile is not successful cellular registration. New foreign-first buyer eligibility remains unverified.

keep.action: Provider currently exposes a Back to China SIM Retention Plan. Community evidence conflicts: some users report roughly 90-day activity for no-plan accounts while plan users follow plan-specific retention. Exact eligibility, current price and post-plan clock are not cleanly provider-reconciled, so no universal interval or annual cost is modeled.

data.chinaActivation: Do NOT infer China-first activation reliability across CTExcel products. One community author describes a £1 physical-SIM Wi-Fi Calling setup using a provider-unsupported network workaround; distinct new annual-eSIM buyers report first activation failed abroad (one in China). No provider-authorized foreign-first tower registration or named-app SMS on a newly bought eSIM has been verified.
data.kyc: Unknown for new purchase. One failed new annual-eSIM owner says support demanded UK passport and selfie for replacement/reissue after failed overseas activation; this is a single disputed recovery-stage report, NOT proof every purchaser needs a UK passport or that Chinese passports are universally rejected.
data.payment: One original purchaser self-reports paying £11 for a promotional annual eSIM; separate annual-eSIM buyer reports starting a bank payment dispute through HSBC Hong Kong. Neither establishes universal checkout pricing, card-country acceptance or buyer residence eligibility. Keep acquisition cost unknown.
data.wifiCalling: One physical-SIM author claims Wi-Fi Calling-based mainland setup only with non-provider-supported network conditions. This is not an approved general China-first eSIM activation route.
data.roamingSms: One physical-SIM setup tutorial claims later mainland cellular signal and general SMS conditional on successful activation. New annual-eSIM buyers report failed first activation; no new eSIM named-app/bank OTP outcome or repeatable success rate is verified.
data.refund: One failed annual-eSIM buyer self-reports support refused a refund and conditioned reissue on UK-passport proof. A second independent annual-eSIM buyer says they opened a bank dispute; final result unreported. These are distinct outcomes, not a proven universal refund policy or successful chargeback.
data.holdReason: HOLD: retention-plan eligibility and 90-day behavior remain unresolved. Two independent new annual-eSIM buyers report overseas first-activation failures; one unofficial physical-SIM Wi-Fi Calling claim is a different cohort. New overseas checkout/KYC, authorized first attach, refunds and named-app OTP are not verified.
data.tariffSummary: Current UK-China plans and retention service exist, but this review intentionally does not publish a single annual keep cost or universal 90-day lifecycle.
guideSteps: Confirm physical SIM versus new annual eSIM product and current authorized first cellular registration country before purchase.
Treat a downloaded eSIM QR/profile as provisioned only; do not infer successful first cellular activation.
Do not rely on unofficial network/geography workarounds as proof of eligible mainland activation.
Check lawful identity, payment and refund/reissue requirements for the exact buyer/channel; one denied-refund and one pending-dispute story are not universal terms.
Keep target service SMS/OTP and long-term renewal reliability unknown until separately verified by independent originals.
